canonical_definition: Video Understanding refers to the general capability of models, particularly large video-language models (LVLMs) and vision-language models (Vid-LLMs), to comprehend video content by analyzing spatial and temporal aspects (objects, actions, events, interactions) and leveraging this understanding to perform tasks such as question answering, captioning, action recognition, temporal localization, and procedural reasoning. While some definitions emphasize fine-grained temporal parsing and object-centric action grounding, others highlight holistic reasoning over long-form temporal dynamics or spatiotemporal information parsing for downstream applications. Consensus centers on the ability to faithfully interpret video data and establish video-language correspondence, often operationalized through benchmarks that test descriptive, predictive, and inferential skills.
